title: AI Chat: choose the model from a list, fewer providers, the mode follows the model, custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenRouter)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Today (v0.26.0): Model is free text. Providers are seven entries: Anthropic, OpenAI Responses, OpenAI Chat, Gemini, Offline local (Ollama), Local Prompt-JSON, Local Q&A (Read-Only), plus an "Offline only" checkbox. Users cannot tell them apart. "Read-only Q&A" is really the fallback mode of a local model without tool calls (`crates/app/src/mcp/fallback.rs`: Native > PromptJson > ReadOnly). It should not be a provider. Lines like "Mode: Native tools · Endpoint: Cloud" are jargon.

Wanted:
1. A model dropdown filled from the provider (the cloud providers' model-list endpoints; Ollama's installed models), typing kept as a fallback.
2. Providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Local (Ollama), Custom OpenAI-compatible (base URL + key, e.g. OpenRouter https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, LM Studio, vLLM). The Prompt-JSON and Read-only modes are picked automatically from the local model's capabilities and shown in plain words ("this model can answer questions but cannot change the project").
3. One plain sentence per provider (where it runs, what it costs, whether it can change the project).

Done means: the user picks provider and model from lists, OpenRouter works through the custom endpoint, and the panel names the mode in plain words. UI structural tests pin the lists and the mode text.

Follows #3781 and #3782.

User validation (reporter, 2026-11-23): before this merges, the reporter (mkinney) hand-tests a build of the PR in the desktop app and confirms it is usable. The PR stays a draft until that confirmation is on the PR.
